description: The bar chart illustrates the task counts across various linguistic categories for mBERT and XLM-R models, as well as tasks where their performance was the same. The horizontal axis lists nine categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, in a fixed order. The vertical axis represents the task count, labeled as "task count," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 40 in intervals of 10. Each category is represented by a group of three bars: mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and 'same' (light green). The task counts for mBERT range from approximately 1 to 12, with the highest value observed in the IE-Romance category and the lowest in IE-Indic and IE-other. XLM-R task counts range from around 6 to 38, with the highest value in the IE-Slavic category. The 'same' task counts range from approximately 1 to 30, with the highest value in the IE-Romance category. The bars are grouped by category, with no specific sorting order within the groups. The legend in the top-right corner clarifies the color coding for the three models.
caption_used: The bar chart compares task counts across linguistic categories for mBERT and XLM-R models, alongside tasks where performance was the same. The horizontal axis lists categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents task count, ranging from 0 to 40. In the IE-Baltic category, XLM-R consistently outperforms mBERT, with task counts exceeding 15. IE-Germanic shows a notable decline in mBERT performance, with task counts below 5, while XLM-R and 'same' are roughly equal at around 20. IE-Slavic demonstrates the highest task count for XLM-R, surpassing 45, while mBERT remains stable at approximately 10 tasks. The Isolate category exhibits minimal variation, with all models performing similarly at around 5 tasks. The legend, located in the top right, clarifies the color coding for mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and 'same' (light green).
